title: Collapse the planning boundary to a single mutation-session contract
description:
A single mutation-session combinator and a fully typed error boundary replace the copy-pasted capture/plan/apply/retry convention and the stringify-then-downcast error handling in the transactional repository-materialization subsystem.

## Background

An adversarial audit of the repository-materialization epic (implementation grade B+, maintainability C+; recorded in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md`) found that the claimed "single planning boundary" is in fact seven public plan-producing entry points across five error types. The capture/plan/apply/retry protocol is hand-copied at 30 sites across 16 command files (29 `for _ in 0..8` loops plus `commands/template.rs:176`) with 65 bespoke `Err(RetryableConflict{..}) => continue` arms and 30 distinct "did not converge" messages; only `template.rs` names its bound. Typed errors round-trip through `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` (34 sites) and are re-typed by the runtime downcast chain in `projection_producer` (`repository_state/mod.rs:590-598`), so exit-code correctness depends on a downcast that silently degrades when a new producer error type appears. The transaction kernel bridges two hand-aligned 4-variant action enums (`RepositoryAction` and `RepositoryJournalActionKind`) with five `unreachable!` panic sites in `storage/file_transaction.rs` that fire mid-publication, after a journal exists. Two of the five `MaterializationRequest` variants (`Initialize`, `ApplyProfile`) return early and never reach the shared plan-identity tail.

The retry sites split into 22 pure single-session loops and 8 self-managed multi-session loops that release a preflight session and then take a `.git/jit` claims guard or run an external subprocess before opening the apply session; a session held across that between-session work would invert lock ordering into a deadlock, so the contract owns the retry bound and conflict classification without holding a session across the closure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A single mutation-session combinator owns the capture/plan/apply/retry protocol — the retry bound, conflict classification, and the terminal conflict error live in one place, and command modules contain no hand-written retry loops or per-site conflict arms. The 30 `for _ in 0..8` loops, 65 `RetryableConflict` arms, and 30 bespoke convergence messages across the 16 command files are retired.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every public plan-producing entry point returns a typed error, and producer failures reach exit-code mapping through typed variants with no stringify-then-downcast round-trip. No function in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` carries an `anyhow` type in its signature, no error value is constructed with `format!`, and `main.rs` maps producer failures through an exhaustive match with no fallback arm.
- [hard] REQ-03: Journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel is total; the publication path contains no `unreachable!` panic sites. The five sites in `storage/file_transaction.rs` (`:759,1079,1088,1097,1104`) return a typed action-mismatch error propagated into the existing non-interruption abort with no partial write.
- [hard] REQ-04: The initialize and profile-application request variants flow through the shared plan-identity tail, or a recorded decision item states why they are exempt.

## Notes

The refactor is behavior-preserving: the existing 35 failure-injection points and ~20 interruption tests must pass unchanged, and conflict-classification unit tests move onto the combinator. REQ-04 may resolve as a recorded exemption decision rather than a code change if the two request variants genuinely cannot share the plan-identity tail.

planning.outcome: A single mutation-session contract and a fully typed error boundary collapse the copy-pasted planning surface.

title: Convert narrated materialization guarantees into enforced tests
description:
Property-based, visibility-based, and contention tests replace narrated guarantees in the repository-materialization subsystem, and well-known repository paths become compile-time constants with repair coverage derived from the repair planner.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found the subsystem's strongest guarantees narrated rather than enforced. The plan-derivation core has zero property-based coverage. The cutover guard is a substring test (`tests/provenance_contract/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:39-66`) that greps four command modules for 14 forbidden literals — defeated by reformatting or by moving a raw write one file over. `ActiveLayoutTracker` (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:79-114`), which rejects reentry under a different layout, has no concurrent test, and there is no multi-threaded stress over `open_mutation_session` contention. Well-known paths are constructed stringly at ~100 fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")` sites, and `tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs:85-108` re-lists 11 repair paths by hand paired with a loose `assert!(count >= 5)`, so a new derived target silently under-covers.

The property targets are `plan_hash` determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip. The visibility replacement tightens the in-repository writers and the `FileTransactionKernel` from `pub(crate)` to `pub(in crate::storage)` so `crate::commands` can no longer name them, retaining the deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions and one narrow retained scan of the four cutover modules for raw `std::fs` publisher calls. `VirtualPath` becomes `Cow<'static, str>`-backed so well-known paths are `pub const` associated items, and a new `repair_target_paths` introspection API on `repository_state` supplies the drift-independent set from which repair coverage is derived.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-05: Property-based tests cover plan-hash determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip.
- [hard] REQ-06: The cutover guard enforces publisher visibility restrictions instead of source-text substring matching, while the deleted-module assertions are retained.
- [hard] REQ-07: Multi-threaded contention tests cover concurrent mutation-session opening and active-layout reentry rejection.
- [hard] REQ-08: Well-known repository file paths are compile-time constants, and repair-path test coverage derives from the repair planner's own declaration rather than a hand-maintained list.

## Notes

Property tests use contract-valid generators and assert observable semantic properties, not copied constants. Contention tests use real threads over a shared `InMemoryStorage` through the public store trait, not failure injection. The suite must not add integration-test targets.

planning.outcome: Property, contention, visibility, and path tests convert narrated materialization guarantees into enforced checks.

title: Establish an artifact-backed performance contract
description:
A checked-in benchmark harness, a bulk-update session-budget fix, and the profile-backed lock-hygiene change turn every published performance figure into an artifact-backed contract.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found every published timing to be a single self-attested measurement with no artifact. `apply_bulk_update` (`commands/bulk_update.rs:161-197`) retains the O(n)-sessions pathology — it opens preflight and publication sessions for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes (cost 2·|matched|) — while `check_auto_transitions` already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap Issue-local eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session. Meanwhile zero-byte `.lock` sidecar files accumulate without bound: `load_issue` shared-locks a `<id>.lock` sidecar on every read (`storage/json.rs:918-919`, created O_CREAT at `storage/lock.rs:286-294`, never removed), so a read-all command such as `jit query available` creates one per issue read (692 sidecars observed for 665 issues).

The lock-hygiene design was decided during planning from the committed session-cost profile `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`: the sidecar originates on the shared read path, so even lazy creation still grows O(issues), and the sidecar read lock is therefore eliminated. Issue JSON is published by atomic temp+rename, writers serialize on `.jit/.repo-write.lock`, and `list_issues` already holds `.index.lock` shared around its load loop, so `load_issue` can read directly (or, as defense-in-depth, take the shared lock on the existing repo-scoped `.index.lock`). The surviving fixed lock set is O(1) — roughly six files independent of issue count — and orphaned sidecars are deleted once as cleanup, not correctness.

The benchmark harness `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository, and times each scenario with warmup and repeated measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` with machine, cache-state, and corpus metadata; `session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template. Every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-09: A checked-in benchmark harness records repeated runs with machine and cache-state metadata as artifacts at a stable path, and every published timing claim traces to such an artifact.
- [hard] REQ-10: Session-open budget tests bound bulk update to eligible work, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions. The bound is C·|matched issues that are not provable no-ops|, with C derived from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoded.
- [hard] REQ-11: The per-session cost profile is recorded as an artifact, and the lock-hygiene approach chosen from that profile is implemented so zero-byte lock files no longer accumulate without bound. The per-issue sidecar read lock is eliminated, the surviving lock set is O(1) in issue count, and orphaned sidecars are cleaned up once.

## Notes

The lock-hygiene decision is pinned by plan decision PD-1: eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock, keep the O(1) fixed lock set, decided from `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`. Every `load_issue` caller must be checked before removing the sidecar lock, since a reader relying on it for more than torn-read protection would be a regression; atomic temp+rename already prevents torn reads. Budget tests count session opens via the existing `TransactionFailurePoint` probe, deterministic and machine-independent. Cache-state contract is warm-only; timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same measurement filesystem.

planning.outcome: A checked-in benchmark harness, a bounded session budget, and lock-hygiene make performance claims artifact-backed.

title: Clear repository-state hygiene debt and document the subsystem
description:
Feature-gating, public-surface reduction, a test-module split and renames, a contributor architecture document, and clearing the recorded advisory debt bring the subsystem's maintainability up to its implementation quality.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` recorded maintainability debt. Test-only API ships in the public library surface: `FailurePoint`/`TransactionFailureInjector`/`NoTransactionFailures` are re-exported at `storage/mod.rs:66-68`, `test_support` (`seed_issue_fixture`) and `test_helpers` are public, and `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` (`storage/json.rs:314`) is a public fault-injection path. Exports are dead or over-broad: `issue_draft` (`mutation.rs:1314`) has zero callers, and 13 further `pub` items have no consumer outside `repository_state`. The repository-state store carries a 3,900-line inline test module (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:1806`), and several tests are named after review rounds (`test_finding2_*`, `test_f2_*`, `test_a1_*`, `test_a5_*`) rather than `test_<function>_<scenario>`. There is no contributor architecture document for the subsystem, and `dev/architecture/core-system-design.md:198-202` still points at a non-existent `docs/storage-abstraction.md`. Four non-lock advisory-debt items remain: `output.rs:433,476`, `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js:161,173,179`, `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3144`, and `scripts/test-ci-manual.sh:66-90`.

The injection seam itself is production code threaded through both storage backends, so the definitions stay unconditional; a `test-support` feature gates only their public exposure, with a `#[cfg(not(feature))] pub(crate)` twin so internal resolution never changes, and tests keep compiling through a self dev-dependency that enables the feature. The public-surface reduction resolves the audit's list as eight demotions to `pub(crate)`, four contract-pinned keeps (the `Contribution` variant payload types behind the `ProfileManifest.contributions` JsonSchema wire contract), three test-only publics (`SerializedRuleSet`/`SchemaFile`/`serialize_ruleset`) moved behind `test-support`, and one deletion. The contributor architecture document lives at `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-12: Test-only failure-injection and fixture surfaces are feature-gated out of the default library surface, dead exports are removed, and public items with no external consumer are demoted to crate visibility.
- [hard] REQ-13: The repository-state store's inline test module lives in a sibling file, and tests named after review rounds follow the `test_<function>_<scenario>` convention.
- [hard] REQ-14: A contributor architecture document covers the repository-state/materialization subsystem, and the stale storage-abstraction pointer in the core system design document is swept.
- [hard] REQ-15: The five advisory-debt items recorded at the predecessor epic's completion are cleared from the codebase and documentation.

## Notes

The feature gating is designed to require no CI or gate-config changes: the self dev-dependency unifies the feature into `cargo test --workspace` while release builds drop the surface, and the standalone `clippy --lib` gate verifies the feature-off public surface. Of REQ-15's five advisory-debt items, four are cleared here; the fifth — the unbounded zero-byte lock files — is cleared by the performance-contract lock-hygiene work and needs no change in this story. The store test split moves a module to a sibling file without adding integration-test targets.

planning.outcome: Feature-gating, surface reduction, test-module hygiene, docs, and debt clearance harden the repository-state subsystem.

title: Replace the repository-materialization showcase with a corrected successor
description:
A corrected successor deck retells the repository-materialization story with every falsifiable claim traced to a repository artifact, and the predecessor deck is archived behind a tombstone.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found nine falsifiable errors in the predecessor showcase deck (`dev/presentations/cdc840ad/talk.html`): a fabricated `fn derive(...)` signature, a non-existent "inspectable" plan JSON document, a "130 session opens" figure that is a 65-issue in-memory model prediction rather than a measurement of this repository, an "independent holistic PASS" that was written by the same agent that built the epic, a `RepositoryImage` struct with a field it does not have, and a diffstat row that reproduces under no stated path filter. It also found the deck loads reveal.js, KaTeX, and three font families from CDNs and cannot present air-gapped, while carrying KaTeX that no slide uses.

The successor deck lives at `dev/presentations/1cc809de/` and re-derives its figures from the performance artifacts and the final tree; every timing cites artifact path, command name, and stat. It carries an explicit correction inventory keyed by audit finding id (A1-1..A1-6, the A2 claims it retells, and A4-1..A4-3), mapping each to its corrected claim and evidence. It ships without KaTeX and with reveal.js and fonts vendored under the deck folder so it presents air-gapped. The predecessor deck moves to `dev/archive/features/cdc840ad/showcase`, leaving a tombstone at the original path that points to the successor deck and the audit.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-16: A corrected successor presentation of the repository-materialization story exists in which every falsifiable claim traces to a repository artifact, and the predecessor deck is archived with a tombstone pointing to the successor and the audit.

## Notes

This deck is a corrected retelling of the predecessor story, not a deck about this epic's own work. Asset vendoring is pinned by plan decision PD-2: reveal.js and fonts are vendored locally and KaTeX is dropped, so rendering is reproducible from the repository alone. The successor must pass the presentation fit checker across all slides.

planning.outcome: A corrected successor deck traces every falsifiable claim to an artifact and the predecessor deck retires behind a tombstone.

title: Self-managed multi-session retry migration
description:
The eight self-managed multi-session retry sites move onto the shared session-free retry driver, keeping their preflight-release-guard-apply structure and lock ordering unchanged.

## Background

Eight command sites run a multi-session retry: within one attempt they release a preflight session and then acquire a `.git/jit` claims guard, run an external checker subprocess, or revalidate a cross-reopen invariant before opening the apply session. The sites are `dependency.rs:260,396`; `issue.rs:552`; `gate.rs:1357`; `mod.rs:2141,2353`; `gate_check.rs:909`; `template.rs:176`. A retry driver that held a session across this between-session work would hold `.repo-write.lock` across `claims_mutation_guard` (inverting today's lock order into a deadlock hazard) and across multi-second subprocess runs, so these sites cannot use a session-holding convenience.

They migrate onto the session-free retry driver:

```rust
fn with_mutation_attempts<T>(operation: &'static str,
    attempt: impl FnMut() -> Result<AttemptOutcome<T>>) -> Result<T>;
enum AttemptOutcome<T> { Done(T), Retry }
```

`with_mutation_attempts` owns the retry bound and the terminal `MutationSessionExhausted` error and holds no session, so the closure opens and releases sessions, takes a claims guard, and runs a subprocess between them exactly as today. Each site keeps its present structure: preflight, release, guard/subprocess, the same cross-reopen equality checks (`template.rs:217-227`; `mod.rs:2430-2444,2491`; `gate_check.rs:997`) returning `Retry`, then apply classified through the shared apply-conflict classifier. Guards are closure locals whose `Drop` runs after apply, preserving lock ordering byte-for-byte.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The eight sites (`dependency.rs:260,396`; `issue.rs:552`; `gate.rs:1357`; `mod.rs:2141,2353`; `gate_check.rs:909`; `template.rs:176`) run their retry through `with_mutation_attempts`; none retains a `for _ in 0..8` loop, a per-site `RetryableConflict` arm, or a bespoke convergence message.
- [hard] REQ-02: The cross-reopen revalidation and lock ordering at each site are unchanged; guards drop after apply exactly as before.
- [hard] REQ-03: After this task no `for _ in 0..8` loop, no `RetryableConflict` match arm, and no bespoke "did not converge" message remains anywhere in the command modules.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing failure-injection and interruption tests pass unchanged; behavior is preserved.

## Notes

This migration consumes the session-free retry driver and shared apply-conflict classifier; those must already exist. Lock ordering must remain byte-for-byte identical: holding `.repo-write.lock` across the claims guard or a subprocess would deadlock.

planning.outcome: The eight self-managed multi-session sites move onto the shared retry driver with lock ordering preserved.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Eight known call sites converted onto the shared driver with lock ordering preserved byte-for-byte.

title: Typed producer and finalizer errors for the repository-state module
description:
Every public plan-producing entry point in the repository-materialization module returns a typed error, replacing the `Producer(String)` stringify-then-downcast round-trip with typed variants that reach exit-code mapping through an exhaustive match.

## Background

Producer failures currently stringify through `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` (34 sites; sink at `repository_state/mod.rs:583` via `format!("{error:#}")`) and are re-typed by a runtime downcast chain `projection_producer` (`mod.rs:590-598`); the exit-code boundary (`main.rs:104,783`) probes with `downcast_ref` + `is_profile_target_conflict`. Exit-code correctness therefore depends on a downcast that silently degrades when a new producer error type appears. This task retypes the whole `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` module.

1. New `ProducerError` (thiserror), each variant carrying its typed source: `MissingCapture(&'static str)`, `MalformedUtf8(#[from] FromUtf8Error)`, `UnknownProjection(String)`, `UnknownKind { projection, kind }`, plus transparent `#[from]` for `CaptureError`, `RepositoryLayoutError`, `ConfigurationDeclarationError`, `InvariantConfigError`, `ItemError`, `RuleConfigError`, `ProjectionError`, `ManagedDocumentError`. The six `materialize.rs` producers (`read_text`, `assemble_config`, `assemble_config_from_declarations`, `render_capture_closure`, `validate_capture_closure`, `compose_configured_projections`) and the two internal `anyhow` leaves - `render_projection_body` (`projection_render.rs:62`, whose injected read-closure becomes `FnMut(&str) -> Result<Option<String>, ProducerError>`) and `validate_proposed_layout` (`artifact_classifier.rs:515`) - return `Result<_, ProducerError>`.
2. `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` becomes `Producer(#[from] ProducerError)`. `fn producer`, `fn projection_producer`, `fn is_profile_target_conflict`, and the twelve `.map_err(...producer...)` sites (`mod.rs:405,415,428,431,436,520,612,617,645,648,678,683`) are deleted in favor of `?`. The inline `Producer(format!)` sites (`mod.rs:501,508`) become `ProducerError::ConfigParse` and a new `RepositoryStateError::Overlay(#[from] OverlayError)`. The profile-application producer (`profile_apply.rs`, `Producer(String)`/`producer` sites at `:397,:435,:469,:678` plus the `profile_registry_error` helper) retypes with profile-specific variants - `ProfileRegistryNotFile { target }`, `ProfileRegistryParse { target, #[source] source }`, `ProfileContributionConflict { identity, registry }`; `compose_default_ruleset` stays as is.
3. `finalize_gate_registry_edit` returns `Result<_, RepositoryStateError>` via a new `GateRegistryEditError { MissingEdit, MultipleEdits, DeclarationMismatch }` variant, with `#[from]` variants for its eight `?`-propagated leaf classes (`MutationError`, `GateDeclarationError`, `OverlayError`, `SeedError` join the existing `Delta`/`PlanHash`/`Layout`).
4. `finalize_archive_execution` returns `Result<_, RepositoryStateError>` via a new `ArchiveExecutionError` enumerating the archive-specific classes at their construction sites - `MissingDestination`, `MissingContentIdentity`, `ContentIdentityChanged`, `NonFileSource{role}`, `UnsafeOccupant{role}`, `MissingPlannedDocument`, `RelinkTargetsPinned`, `RelinkStale`, `MissingCapturedIssue`, `MalformedIssueJson(#[source] serde_json::Error)`, `IssueIdMismatch`, `CapturedIssueCacheLost`, `MissingChangedIssue` - plus `#[from]` for its typed leaves (`EventLogError`, `PlanError`, the retyped `validate_proposed_layout`).
5. `main.rs::error_to_exit_code` replaces the two downcast probes with one exhaustive match over `RepositoryStateError` (no `_ =>` arm): projection/managed-document/profile-conflict/ambiguous-ownership/gate-registry-edit/archive-execution variants map to the validation-failed exit; capture/parse producer variants to the generic exit; layout variants to the invalid-argument exit. The profile `--json` boundary keeps its single sanctioned `downcast_ref::<RepositoryStateError>` on the anyhow CLI transport, but `profile_json_error` (`main.rs:770-791`) matches the `ProfileTargetConflict` variant instead of the deleted `is_profile_target_conflict` bool (new profile producer variants map to `PROFILE_CONFLICT`/`PROFILE_ERROR` codes explicitly).

Acceptance is module-wide, not per enumerated site: (a) no function in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` carries an `anyhow` type in its signature; (b) no error value is constructed with `format!`, and `String`-typed variant fields carry raw identifiers (a projection name, a registry target) captured by value, never a pre-rendered message - all rendering lives in `Display` impls.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `ProducerError` exists with the variants above; `RepositoryStateError::Producer` carries `#[from] ProducerError`; `fn producer`, `fn projection_producer`, and `fn is_profile_target_conflict` are deleted and their former callers use `?`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `finalize_gate_registry_edit` and `finalize_archive_execution` return typed `RepositoryStateError` values via the new `GateRegistryEditError` and `ArchiveExecutionError` types.
- [hard] REQ-03: No function in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` carries an `anyhow` type in its signature.
- [hard] REQ-04: No error value in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` is constructed with `format!`; `String`-typed error-variant fields hold raw identifiers, and all message rendering lives in `Display` impls.
- [hard] REQ-05: `main.rs::error_to_exit_code` maps producer failures through an exhaustive match over `RepositoryStateError` with no fallback (`_ =>`) arm.
- [hard] REQ-06: Existing behavior and exit codes are preserved; the failure-path tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

Scope is the whole `repository_state` module: beyond the enumerated surfaces, retire every remaining `anyhow` signature and `format!`-constructed error value in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/`, including the export, initialization, and profile-application paths, because criteria (a)/(b) are checked module-wide. The exhaustive `main.rs` match owned here must also carry an arm for the command layer's mutation-session terminal error (contributed by the retry-contract work) so it stays exhaustive; the finalizer signature changes compose through the command modules' unchanged anyhow boundary.

planning.outcome: Producer and finalizer failures become typed, so exit-code mapping needs no stringify-then-downcast round-trip.

terminal.test_boundary: compiler totality plus exit-code mapping tests

title: Total journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel
description:
Journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel becomes total: the five `unreachable!` panic sites in the publication path return a typed action-mismatch error that propagates into the existing non-interruption abort with no partial write.

## Background

The transaction kernel bridges two hand-aligned 4-variant action enums - `RepositoryAction` (semantic intent) and `RepositoryJournalActionKind` (staging control-names) - with five `unreachable!` panic sites in `crates/jit/src/storage/file_transaction.rs` (`:759,1079,1088,1097,1104`) that fire mid-publication, after a journal exists. The two enums carry genuinely disjoint payloads, so they stay separate types. Retype the four alignment extractors and the `SetMode`-preimage destructure (`:1079,1088,1097,1104` and `:759`) to return a new `FileTransactionError::JournalActionMismatch { index, expected, found }` over a shared 4-value `ActionTag`, instead of `unreachable!`.

All five sites propagate with `?` into the existing non-interruption abort (cleanup then error, no partial write, `file_transaction.rs:866-876`):
- The four extractor sites (`:1079-:1104`) already sit inside the prepare loop that the abort handler wraps, so `?` reaches the abort directly.
- The `:759` journal-construction site runs after transaction control has been created but before a complete journal exists, so it routes through a control-only teardown: factor the `ControlDirs` removal tail of `cleanup_repository_control` into its own function that skips the journal-dependent data-stage steps (provably no-ops before prepare stages anything), so a mismatch tears down the created control immediately instead of leaving it for later recovery.

Durable journal decode corruption stays with the existing serde and `ControlName` validation paths.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/storage/file_transaction.rs` contains no `unreachable!` in the publication path; the five sites (`:759,1079,1088,1097,1104`) return `FileTransactionError::JournalActionMismatch { index, expected, found }` over a shared `ActionTag`.
- [hard] REQ-02: All five sites propagate with `?` into the existing non-interruption abort, leaving no partial write; the `:759` site tears down created control through the factored control-only teardown that skips journal-dependent data-stage steps.
- [hard] REQ-03: `RepositoryAction` and `RepositoryJournalActionKind` remain separate types with their disjoint payloads.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing interruption tests pass unchanged; behavior is preserved.

## Notes

File ownership for this task is `crates/jit/src/storage/file_transaction.rs` and `crates/jit/src/storage/transaction_journal.rs`.

planning.outcome: Journal-action extraction returns a typed mismatch error instead of unreachable panics on the publication path.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Five extractor sites retyped to a mismatch error routed through the existing abort path.

title: Plan-identity tail for initialize and profile-application requests
description:
The initialize and profile-application materialization request variants either flow through the shared plan-identity tail or a recorded decision item states why they are exempt.

## Background

The transaction kernel routes `MaterializationRequest` variants through a shared plan-identity tail, but two of them - `Initialize` and `ApplyProfile` - return early and never reach that tail. Either fold both variants into the shared plan-identity tail, or, if they genuinely cannot share it, record a decision item stating why they are exempt. Either outcome satisfies the requirement; the exemption route requires a durable recorded decision with its rationale, not an undocumented early return.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `Initialize` and `ApplyProfile` request variants flow through the shared plan-identity tail, or a recorded decision item states, with its rationale, why they are exempt.
- [hard] REQ-02: If the exemption route is taken, the decision is captured as a durable recorded item rather than left as an unexplained early return.

## Notes

Prefer folding the two variants into the shared tail; take the exemption only if the plan-identity tail genuinely cannot be reached for these request kinds.

planning.outcome: Initialize and profile-application requests share the plan-identity tail, or a recorded decision states the exemption.

title: Property tests for plan-hash determinism and managed-document splice
description:
Add property-based tests, with contract-valid generators, covering plan-hash determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip in the repository-materialization subsystem.

## Background

The plan-derivation core of the repository-materialization subsystem currently has zero property-based coverage; its strongest guarantees are narrated rather than enforced. `RepositoryDelta::new` normalization/alias rejection (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:1266`), `plan_hash` determinism (`image.rs:1385`), and managed-document splice round-trip are the textbook property targets and the headline claim.

Two properties are in scope, each driven by a `proptest` generator that produces only contract-valid inputs and an oracle that asserts an observable semantic property (not a copied constant):

**Plan-hash determinism under action reordering.** Generate distinct-path action sets: a `btree_set` of `VirtualPath` mapped to actions whose preimage matches the kind per `validate_action`, with a path-derived unique `EntryIdentity` so the physical-alias check is cleared. Because `RepositoryDelta::new` sorts its input and rejects duplicates, reordering is a boundary phenomenon: the oracle permutes the input order, builds two deltas through `RepositoryDelta::new`, and asserts `plan_hash` equality across the permutations. A discriminating half of the generator asserts `plan_hash` equality holds **iff** the two normalized deltas are equal, so the test cannot pass by collapsing distinct inputs.

**Managed-document splice round-trip.** Generate N region claims with unique, machine-distinct delimiters and content/outside bytes drawn from a delimiter-free alphabet (so `validate_regions` accepts them), interleaved into a base document per placement mode. The oracle goes through the public `render_managed_document` only and asserts the three round-trip properties: rendering is idempotent, each region's payload appears verbatim inside its region, and bytes outside all regions are unchanged.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A property-based test asserts `plan_hash` is invariant under permutation of the action set's input order, built through `RepositoryDelta::new`, with a discriminating case that ties hash equality to normalized-delta equality.
- [hard] REQ-02: A property-based test asserts the managed-document splice round-trip through the public `render_managed_document`: rendering is idempotent, each generated region's payload appears verbatim within its region, and bytes outside all regions are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Generators produce only contract-valid inputs (action preimages matching their kind with unique `EntryIdentity`; regions satisfying `validate_regions`), and every assertion is a semantic property or relationship rather than a copied literal or field inventory.

## Notes

Use `proptest`. The suite must not add any integration-test target; place the property tests in an in-crate test module. Assert observable semantic properties per the project's semantic-test-assertions invariant, not exact hash values or copied constants.

planning.outcome: Property tests pin plan-hash determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip.

title: Visibility-enforced cutover guard
description:
Replace the source-text substring cutover guard with a compile-time visibility restriction so only the mutation-session API can publish into repository roots, retaining the deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions.

## Background

The current cutover guard is the substring test at `crates/jit/tests/provenance_contract/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:39-67`. It greps the production halves of the four cutover command modules for ~14 forbidden substrings (for example `"std::fs::write("`, `"OpenOptions::new("`, `"atomic_write"`), splitting production from test source on the literal `"\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod "`. This enforces the narrative, not a property: it breaks on reformatting and is defeated by moving a raw write one file over. The property it approximates is that only the mutation-session API may publish into repository roots.

The visibility replacement makes that property compiler-enforced:

- `FileTransactionKernel` (and `TransactionControlLocation`) and the in-repository writers `write_file_atomic` / `write_file_atomic_bytes` tighten from `pub(crate)` to `pub(in crate::storage)`. Their only callers -- `repository_state_store.rs`, `user_config_store.rs`, `file_transaction.rs` -- live in `crate::storage`, so repository-owned publishers compile unchanged while `crate::commands` can no longer name them.
- The three external-export wrappers `write_external_export_atomic`, `publish_external_file_noreplace`, and `publish_external_directory_noreplace` move into a new `storage::external_publish` submodule re-exported `pub(crate)`. Their legitimate callers `commands/snapshot.rs` and `commands/graph.rs` publish to caller-chosen paths outside repository roots (charter D-4), and the module name states that intent.
- The low-level rename primitive `rename_noreplace_cap` is a repository transaction primitive, not an export API: it stays `pub(in crate::storage)` alongside the in-repository writers, reachable by the external-publish wrappers only through their storage-internal implementation.

Residual raw `std::fs` publishing cannot be restricted by visibility, so one narrow assertion is retained in the same provenance-contract suite: it scans **only** the four cutover command modules for the four raw `std::fs` publisher calls (`fs::write`, `fs::rename`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions::new`). This is a deliberate, recorded exception to the visibility mechanism. A crate-wide `clippy.toml` disallowed-methods rule is rejected because `commands/snapshot.rs` legitimately stages exports with raw `std::fs` into temp directories.

The deleted-module and renderer-owner tests in the same file (`:69-139` and `:141-161`) are retained verbatim; only the substring test is deleted.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The cutover guard enforces publisher visibility (`pub(in crate::storage)` on `FileTransactionKernel`, `TransactionControlLocation`, `write_file_atomic`, `write_file_atomic_bytes`, and `rename_noreplace_cap`; external-export wrappers relocated to a `pub(crate)` `storage::external_publish` submodule) instead of source-text substring matching, and the substring test is removed.
- [hard] REQ-02: The deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions in the provenance-contract suite are retained unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: `crate::commands` cannot name the tightened publishers (the build fails if it does), while `repository_state_store.rs`, `user_config_store.rs`, `file_transaction.rs`, `commands/snapshot.rs`, and `commands/graph.rs` compile against their permitted surfaces unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: One narrow assertion remains in the provenance-contract suite scanning only the four cutover command modules for the four raw `std::fs` publisher calls (`fs::write`, `fs::rename`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions::new`).

## Notes

Do not introduce a crate-wide `clippy.toml` disallowed-methods rule; `commands/snapshot.rs` uses raw `std::fs` legitimately for temp-directory export staging. The suite must not add any integration-test target.

title: Multi-threaded contention tests for mutation sessions and layout reentry
description:
Add multi-threaded contention tests covering concurrent mutation-session opening and active-layout reentry rejection, using real threads over a shared in-memory store through the public store trait.

## Background

`ActiveLayoutTracker` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:79-114`) rejects reentry under a different layout but has no concurrent test, and there is no multi-threaded stress over `open_mutation_session` contention. - **Concurrent `open_mutation_session`** -- multiple threads race to open mutation sessions against the shared store; the test asserts the observable serialization/conflict behavior surfaced by the public API.
- **Active-layout reentry rejection** -- reentry under a different layout is observed as the `RetryableConflict` that `ActiveLayoutTracker::enter` surfaces through the store trait, under concurrent access.

- [hard] REQ-03: The contention tests use real threads over a shared store through the public trait, with no failure injection, and reside in a new in-crate `repository_state_store_contention_tests` module added via its own `mod` declaration.

title: Compile-time path constants and derived repair-path coverage
description:
Make well-known repository file paths compile-time constants and derive repair-path test coverage from the repair planner's own declaration instead of a hand-maintained list.

## Background

`VirtualPath` is `String`-backed through `RootRelativePath::Descendant(String)` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:13-19`), which blocks `const`. There are ~100 production `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` call sites (for example `gates.toml`, `events.jsonl`, `config.toml`, `index.json`, `rules.toml`), each a fallible construction of a compile-time-known-good value.

**Path constants.** Change the payload to `Cow<'static, str>`. `Cow::Borrowed` is const-constructible, so well-known paths become `pub const` associated items (`VirtualPath::GATES`, `EVENTS`, `CONFIG`, `INDEX`, `RULES`, ...) and the fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` sites become infallible const references. Parsing and deserialization produce `Cow::Owned`; `Ord`/`Hash`/`Eq` semantics are unchanged (`Borrowed("x") == Owned("x")`), so const and parsed keys collide correctly in the `BTreeMap`-keyed image. Because consts bypass the reserved-path `checked()` guard (`path.rs:173-186`), one test iterates every associated const via a `VirtualPath::ALL_KNOWN` list, asserting round-trip equality through the fallible constructor -- proving each const canonical and non-reserved.

**Derived repair coverage.** The repair test at `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs:85-110` re-lists 11 repair paths by hand as `repair_paths()`, paired with a loose `assert!(count >= 5)`, so a new derived target silently under-covers. Two facts shape the fix: every family in `derive_repair` (`repository_state/mod.rs:660-701`) is drift-filtered -- projections skip when bytes already match (`materialize.rs:351-357`), the default ruleset writes only on diff (`materialize.rs:432,456-459`), profile targets push only when the entry differs (`mod.rs:680-697`) -- so a set derived from walked actions would enumerate only currently-drifting paths; and the 11 literals mix repair write-targets with three fixture-input-only paths (`index.json`, `events.jsonl`, the profile record) that `derive_repair` never writes.

Add a new public introspection API `repository_state::repair_target_paths(image, declarations, profiles) -> Result<BTreeSet<VirtualPath>>` that enumerates the complete drift-independent set of paths repair may materialize: default-ruleset targets guarded by the capture spec (via `serialized_default_ruleset(config).schema_files`), configured-projection targets (via `require_target`), and the keys of `compose_profile_targets` per claims. Obsolete-schema deletions stay excluded by definition -- their targets are occupant-proven paths deliberately outside the declared set (`materialize.rs:498-512`). `derive_repair` is **not** refactored to consume it (it needs composed bytes per target, which a path set cannot supply); instead the authority relationship is enforced by a unit test asserting every non-delete action target of `derive_repair` is a member of `repair_target_paths` on the same inputs. The repair test's hand-list is replaced by `repair_paths() = repair_target_paths(...) union {index.json, events.jsonl, profile record}` (the three fixture-input paths as an explicit tail), and it gains a full-drift coverage assertion: seed every target stale and assert the repair delta's write/set-mode target set equals `repair_target_paths(...)` exactly.

`repair_target_paths` is an ordinary public API of `repository_state` -- a declarative introspection surface in the same spirit as validation -- so both the in-crate subset test and the integration coverage test call it without `test-support` gating.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `VirtualPath` is `Cow<'static, str>`-backed and the well-known repository paths are `pub const` associated items, replacing the ~100 fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` construction sites with infallible const references, with `Ord`/`Hash`/`Eq` semantics preserved so const and parsed keys collide correctly.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test iterates every associated const via `VirtualPath::ALL_KNOWN` and asserts round-trip equality through the fallible constructor, proving each const canonical and non-reserved.
- [hard] REQ-03: A public `repository_state::repair_target_paths(image, declarations, profiles) -> Result<BTreeSet<VirtualPath>>` enumerates the drift-independent repair-target set (default-ruleset targets, configured-projection targets, profile-target keys; obsolete-schema deletions excluded), and a unit test asserts every non-delete `derive_repair` action target is a member of `repair_target_paths` on the same inputs.
- [hard] REQ-04: The repair test replaces its hand-maintained list with `repair_target_paths(...)` plus the three explicit fixture-input paths, and asserts under full seeded drift that the repair delta's write/set-mode target set equals `repair_target_paths(...)` exactly.

## Notes

Both the subset unit test and the full-drift coverage test call `repair_target_paths` without any `test-support` feature gating and with no dependency on the feature-gating hygiene task. The suite must not add any integration-test target.

planning.outcome: Well-known paths become compile-time constants and repair coverage derives from the repair planner's declaration.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Cow-backed path payload with const associated items and one derived repair-coverage authority.

title: Benchmark harness and first session-cost artifact
description:
Add a checked-in benchmark harness that records repeated timing runs as JSON artifacts at a stable repository path, so every published performance figure traces to an artifact instead of a single self-attested measurement.

## Background

Today every published timing is a lone, un-artifacted measurement. This task adds `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh`, modeled on the existing `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. The script builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and times each scenario with at least 3 warmup runs and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` — the jit commit in the filename so history accumulates. The committed `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template the harness must reproduce.

Artifact schema (top-level keys): `schema_version`; `jit{version,commit,dirty,profile}`; `machine{cpu_model,logical_cpus,ram_kb,kernel,measurement_fs,repo_real_fs}`; `corpus{issue_count}`; `method{samples_per_command,warmup_runs,warm,cache_state,timing_clock}`; `commands[]{name,argv,class,n,min_ms,median_ms,p95_ms,max_ms,lock_files_created}`; and `mutation_syscall_summary{task_clock_ms,user_s,sys_s,page_faults,context_switches}`.

Scenarios in the `commands` array: baseline (`--version`), single read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single mutation (`issue update --priority`). The bulk-mutation scenario is intentionally excluded here; it is added later, once the bulk-update fix lands, so its numbers measure the fixed behavior.

Mutable scenarios need a reset protocol: the harness materializes a fresh fixture repository per measured sample (regenerate, or restore from a pristine copy) so no sample observes a prior sample's mutations; warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.

Cache-state contract is warm-only: cold-cache measurement needs root to drop the page cache and is not assumed; warm means the page cache is primed by warmup runs against the pristine copy. Timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same `measurement_fs`.

Citation rule: every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat (for example `session-cost-<commit>.json > issue_update_mutation > median_ms`); an uncited number is a staleness defect.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` is checked in, builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and for each scenario runs at least 3 warmup and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The emitted artifact conforms to the schema of `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`: the same top-level keys (`schema_version`, `jit`, `machine`, `corpus`, `method`, `commands`) and the same per-command stat fields (`name`, `argv`, `class`, `n`, `min_ms`, `median_ms`, `p95_ms`, `max_ms`, `lock_files_created`).
- [hard] REQ-03: The `commands` array covers the baseline (`--version`), single-read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single-mutation (`issue update --priority`) scenarios, and contains no bulk-mutation scenario.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each mutable scenario runs against a freshly materialized fixture per measured sample so no sample observes a prior sample's mutation, and warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.
- [hard] REQ-05: The artifact records machine identity (cpu model, logical cpus, ram, kernel, measurement filesystem, real-repo filesystem) and a warm-only cache-state field.
- [hard] REQ-06: Any performance timing stated in repository prose or documentation cites artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Notes

Model the script structure on `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. Timing figures are machine-specific; record machine identity rather than asserting portability. Do not hardcode expected millisecond values in tests — the artifact is the contract, not any single number.

planning.outcome: A checked-in harness records repeated timed runs as JSON artifacts at a stable per-commit path.

title: Bulk-update eligibility prefilter and session-budget test
description:
Bound `apply_bulk_update` session opens to the matched issues that actually need a change, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions, and extend the benchmark harness with a bulk-mutation scenario measuring the fixed behavior.

## Background

`apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`, roughly lines 161-197) currently opens a preflight session and a publication session for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes — cost 2·|matched|. `check_auto_transitions` already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap in-memory eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session.

The fix adds a pure `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop(&Issue) -> bool` prefilter over the already-listed issues. It is deliberately Issue-local and no-op-only: it skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds (state equal, labels present/absent, priority, gate and assignee state), all decidable from the listed `Issue` alone. Potentially invalid updates are not prefiltered — they still open sessions so the same authoritative in-session validation produces the same per-issue error results as today. Repository-dependent validity never moves out of the session, and the prefilter only skips, never authorizes (the same TOCTOU-safe property as the auto-transitions guard).

The session-open bound: sessions opened = C·|{matched issues that are not provable no-ops}|, where C is the per-mutation session constant (currently 2: preflight plus publication). The budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, so later combinator refactors cannot invalidate it. The test reuses the same session-open counting probe the auto-transitions budget test uses (`test_check_auto_transitions_opens_sessions_only_for_eligible_backlog_issues` in `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs`), which counts the once-per-session-open failure point. It seeds K matched issues of which K-J already hold their target values and asserts C·J session opens, not C·K.

After the fix lands, the benchmark harness `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` gains a bulk-mutation scenario (a filtered `issue update`) recorded in the artifact's `commands` array, so the artifact captures the fixed behavior.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops; for K matched issues of which J require a change, session opens equal C·J where C is the per-mutation session constant.
- [hard] REQ-02: `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop` is a pure, Issue-local predicate that skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds; it never authorizes an update and never moves repository-dependent validity out of the session.
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue whose update is potentially invalid still opens a session and yields the same per-issue error result as before the change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The session-budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, and asserts C·J for K seeded issues with K-J already at their target values.
- [hard] REQ-05: The benchmark harness records a bulk-mutation scenario in its artifact, measuring the post-fix behavior.

## Notes

The fix is behavior-preserving for update results: only the number of sessions opened for provable no-ops changes. Do not hardcode C; a single-issue baseline run yields it.

planning.outcome: Bulk update opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops, with a session-budget test.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure Issue-local predicate plus one session-budget test derived from a baseline run.

title: Lock-hygiene: eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock
description:
Eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock so zero-byte `.lock` files no longer accumulate without bound, keep the surviving fixed lock set O(1) in issue count, and clean up orphaned sidecars once.

## Background

Zero-byte `.lock` sidecar files accumulate without bound. `load_issue` takes a shared lock on a `<id>.lock` sidecar on every read (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs`, around lines 918-919), created with `O_CREAT` at `crates/jit/src/storage/lock.rs` (around lines 286-294) and never removed. A read-all command such as `jit query available` therefore creates one sidecar per issue read (692 sidecars observed for 665 issues).

The pinned decision (PD-1) is to eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock. It is redundant: issue JSON is published by atomic temp-file-plus-rename, so a reader can never observe a torn file; writers serialize on `.jit/.repo-write.lock`; and `list_issues` already holds the repo-scoped `.index.lock` shared around its load loop. `load_issue` can therefore read directly, or, as defense-in-depth, take the shared lock on the existing repo-scoped `.index.lock` instead of a per-issue sidecar. The surviving fixed lock set is O(1) — roughly six files independent of issue count (`.repo-write`, `.index`, `.gates`, `.events`, the per-worktree bootstrap lock, and the claims lock). Retained fixed locks stay `O_CREAT` without `O_EXCL` and are never unlinked, so flock coordination remains race-safe. Orphaned sidecars are deleted once as cleanup, not correctness.

Every existing `load_issue` caller must be checked before removing the lock: a reader that relied on the sidecar for more than torn-read protection would be a regression, and atomic temp-plus-rename already prevents torn reads.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The per-issue sidecar read lock in `load_issue` is eliminated; no read path creates a per-`<id>.lock` sidecar file.
- [hard] REQ-02: After a command that reads every issue, the number of lock files that exist is O(1) in issue count — the surviving fixed lock set is independent of the number of issues.
- [hard] REQ-03: Orphaned zero-byte sidecar `.lock` files are removed once as a cleanup step.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every existing `load_issue` caller is confirmed not to depend on the sidecar lock for anything beyond torn-read protection, which atomic temp-file-plus-rename already provides.
- [hard] REQ-05: This clears the outstanding zero-byte-lock advisory-debt item.

## Notes

The per-session cost profile artifact half of this contract is already committed at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`; do not regenerate or duplicate it here. Retained fixed locks must keep their current `O_CREAT`-without-`O_EXCL` creation and must not be unlinked, so flock coordination stays race-safe.

planning.outcome: Removing the per-issue sidecar read lock keeps the surviving fixed lock set O(1) in issue count.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Remove one read-path lock, keep the fixed lock set, and clean orphaned sidecars once.

title: Feature-gate the test-support library surface
description:
Introduce a `test-support` Cargo feature that removes test-only failure-injection and fixture APIs from the default library surface while leaving their definitions and all internal resolution unchanged.

## Background

The fault-injection seam is production code, not test scaffolding: `storage/file_transaction.rs` threads `&dyn TransactionFailureInjector` through ~121 `repository_check` sites, and both storage backends hold an `Arc<dyn TransactionFailureInjector>` that defaults to `NoTransactionFailures`. The definitions therefore stay unconditional; only their *public exposure* is gated.

A `test-support` feature in `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` gates each of these public exposures, in every case keeping a feature-off twin so nothing inside the crate changes how it resolves the symbol:

- The sole public re-export of `FailurePoint as TransactionFailurePoint`, `TransactionFailureInjector`, and `NoTransactionFailures` at `crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:66-68`. Under the feature it stays `pub use`; without it, a `#[cfg(not(feature = "test-support"))] pub(crate) use` twin exposes the same names crate-internally so internal callers resolve identically.
- `mod test_support` (the `seed_issue_fixture` helper, which uses `.expect()` calls unfit for shipped library code).
- `pub mod test_helpers`, currently `#[cfg(test)]` at `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:64`, widened to `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`.
- The conflict-injection branch at `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:527-532` plus its `memory.rs` backing machinery: change `#[cfg(test)]` to `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]`.
- The file backend's only public fault-injection path, `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` at `crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:314`, with the same feature-on-`pub` / feature-off-`pub(crate)` twin.

The memory backend's injection twins are already `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` and need no change.

Tests keep compiling through a self dev-dependency: add `[dev-dependencies] jit = { path = ".", features = ["test-support"] }` to `crates/jit/Cargo.toml`, and enable the same feature on `crates/server`'s `jit` dev-dependency. This unifies the feature into `cargo test --workspace` while `cargo build` and release builds drop the surface. No integration-test target is added, and no CI or gate configuration changes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `test-support` feature is declared in `crates/jit/Cargo.toml`. With the feature disabled, none of `TransactionFailurePoint`, `TransactionFailureInjector`, `NoTransactionFailures`, `seed_issue_fixture`/`test_support`, `test_helpers`, or `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` is reachable from the crate's public API (each is `pub(crate)`, `#[cfg]`-excluded, or otherwise non-`pub`).
- [hard] REQ-02: With the feature enabled, those same items are public exactly as before, and the injection-seam definitions compile unconditionally in both feature states.
- [hard] REQ-03: Crate-internal resolution of every gated symbol is identical whether or not the feature is on (the feature-off twins preserve `pub(crate)` visibility for internal callers).
- [hard] REQ-04: `cargo test --workspace` compiles and passes with no added `--features` argument, because the self dev-dependency and the `crates/server` dev-dependency enable `test-support` for test builds.
- [hard] REQ-05: `cargo clippy --lib` on the default (feature-off) surface reports zero warnings, and no new integration-test target is introduced.

Each must be renamed to `test_<function>_<scenario>` describing the function and scenario it exercises; the existing scenario suffixes already indicate the behavior and can seed the new names.

title: Clear the four non-lock advisory-debt items
description:
Resolve the four non-lock advisory-debt items recorded at the predecessor epic's completion: a dead output parameter, noisy MCP schema-generator warnings, a mismatched CLI error-code doc, and a fail-open manual CI script.

## Background

The predecessor epic's completion report recorded five advisory-debt items. Four of them, none touching lock files, are cleared here (the fifth, unbounded zero-byte lock files, is cleared by the performance-contract lock-hygiene work and needs no change here).

1. **Dead output parameter.** `JsonOutput::success` (`crates/jit/src/output.rs:433`) and `JsonError::new` (`crates/jit/src/output.rs:476`) each accept an unused `_command: impl Into<String>` parameter explicitly "kept for API compatibility." This is a greenfield repository where compatibility is not required, so the parameter and the argument passed at every call site are stale ceremony to remove.

2. **Noisy MCP schema generator.** The `$ref` resolver in `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js` emits `console.error` warnings for circular references (line 161), missing definitions (line 173), and unrecognized `$ref` formats (line 179). MCP schema tests pass but emit numerous unresolved-definition and circular-reference warnings; their volume can hide new regressions. Fix the cause at the generator boundary so generation resolves cleanly rather than suppressing the warning calls.

3. **Mismatched CLI error-code doc.** `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3144` states that a failing `project render` under `--json` returns code `PROJECT_COMMAND_FAILED`, while typed validation and projection failures actually surface `VALIDATION_FAILED` (as documented elsewhere in the same file). The reference must describe the typed error-code split as implemented instead of claiming one blanket code.

4. **Fail-open manual CI script.** `scripts/test-ci-manual.sh:66-90` skips the Cargo security audit when `cargo-audit` is absent and converts npm-audit failures into warnings, yet the script still ends by printing "All CI checks complete." It is fail-open and must not resolve to a success outcome while a security audit is skipped or failing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The unused `_command` parameter is removed from `JsonOutput::success` and `JsonError::new` in `crates/jit/src/output.rs` and from every call site; the JSON output types build and produce identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: MCP schema generation through `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js` completes without emitting circular-reference, missing-definition, or unrecognized-`$ref` warnings, with the cause fixed at the generator boundary rather than the warning calls suppressed, and `npm test` in `mcp-server/` passes.
- [hard] REQ-03: `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` describes the typed error-code split for `project render` under `--json` - validation/projection failures surface `VALIDATION_FAILED` - instead of stating a single `PROJECT_COMMAND_FAILED` at line 3144, matching the code's actual behavior.
- [hard] REQ-04: `scripts/test-ci-manual.sh` no longer reports success while a security audit is skipped or failing: a missing `cargo-audit` tool or a non-clean `cargo audit` or `npm audit` no longer resolves to the "All CI checks complete" outcome.

## Notes

The four items span Rust, the MCP server, and documentation, so this task carries the union of those footprints' gates.

**A1 corrections (must-fix falsifiable errors):**

- **A1-1** The predecessor's `fn derive(...)` signature is fabricated; no `derive` function exists. The real closed entry point is `pub fn derive_materialization(image: &RepositoryImage, request: MaterializationRequest<'_>) -> Result<MaterializationPlan, RepositoryStateError>` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:422-425`). `MaterializationRequest` is a closed 5-variant enum (`SemanticMutation`, `RenderConfiguredProjections`, `RepairDerivedState`, `Initialize`, `ApplyProfile`); the return is fallible.

The only genuinely inspectable JSON is `jit profile apply --dry-run`, which emits `ProfilePlanResult { id, version, status, plan_hash, targets }` (`crates/jit/src/profile/application.rs:139-151`). Either drop the JSON block or relabel it as the real profile-apply dry-run shape.
- **A1-3** The current-repository-produced-130-session-opens figure is false: 130 is a prediction from a 65-issue in-memory model, not a measurement of this repository, and it is never shown in a table headed as measured. State it as prediction, e.g. a 65-issue deterministic model predicts 130 session opens for the old path; the corrected path opens 2. The post-fix 2 is genuinely measured by `test_check_auto_transitions_opens_sessions_only_for_eligible_backlog_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs`).
- **A1-4** Independent holistic PASS was written by the same building agent and no `holistic` gate existed for the predecessor. Do not describe the predecessor self-review as independent. If an independence claim is made, it must cite the actually-independent holistic review performed for the current hardening epic by a reviewer distinct from the building agent.
- **A1-5** The `RepositoryImage` struct shown has a field it does not have (`evidence: RepositoryRootEvidence`). The real fields are `layout`, `spec`, `entries`, `listings`, `pinned`, `linked_worktree` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:599-607`); `RepositoryRootEvidence` lives two levels down inside `RepositoryLayout`.
- **A1-6** The Product-plus-public-docs +48,974 / -23,996 diffstat row reproduces under no stated path filter. **Timing-citation rule.** Every timing figure in the deck cites its source as artifact path + command name + statistic, for example `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<commit>.json > issue_update_mutation > median_ms`. Performance artifacts live at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` and carry per-command stats under `commands[]{name, min_ms, median_ms, p95_ms, max_ms}`.
